1 The diskproxy manual

diskproxy presents a folder to macOS applications as a virtual disk, an NFS volume or a WebDAV share, without ever writing to the folder. A plugin decides what the application sees: which files are visible, which timestamps they carry, how each file’s bytes are put together, and what happens to metadata the application writes back. Source bytes are read on demand, and disk metadata is built in memory, so nothing is copied and no kernel extension, FUSE driver or Python runtime is needed.

This manual is for people who want to use diskproxy, and for developers who want to adapt it. It covers installation, everyday commands, every configuration key, the three transports, writable views, two complete workflows, writing a plugin, the internal architecture, limits and troubleshooting. The README is the short version; the project story explains how the design came about.
